case_title: Beere Gowda v. State of Karnataka
aggravating_circumstances: Forcible administration of acid, intent to kill, domestic abuse
neutral_facts: The accused, Beere Gowda, and his co-accused, Indramma, were involved in the death of a two-and-a-half-year-old child, Pallavi. Pallavi was the daughter of Beere Gowda and his first wife, Jayanthi. After a marital dispute, Beere Gowda married Indramma. The prosecution alleged that Beere Gowda and Indramma intentionally administered a mixture of nitric and sulphuric acid to Pallavi, leading to her death. An FIR was lodged by Jayanthi, and Beere Gowda was arrested. A bottle containing the mixture was found in his home. The trial court acquitted both accused, but the High Court overturned the acquittal and convicted Beere Gowda under Section 302 of the IPC. Medical evidence indicated that the acid was forcibly administered, as injuries were found on multiple parts of the body, suggesting the child fought back.
